---
title: "Cobb-Douglas production function"
page-layout: full
toc: false
---

{{< include _sequence.qmd >}}

A Cobb-Douglas production function gives output $q$ from labour $L$ and capital $K$:

$$
q = f(L, K) = A L^a K^b .
$$

An isoquant shows all the combinations of labour and capital that produce the same
quantity of output. The chart draws the isoquants for fixed quantities,
$q = 2, 4, 6, \ldots$, so you can see how they move as the parameters change.
Raising $A$ shifts every isoquant in towards the origin: the same output needs
fewer inputs. The exponents $a$ and $b$ set how productive each input is, which
changes the slope of the isoquants, and their sum determines returns to scale.
Switch on constant returns to scale to set $b = 1 - a$, so that
$q = A L^a K^{1-a}$.

The [next page](cost.qmd) adds the costs of labour and capital, and finds the
cheapest way to produce a given quantity.

::: {.sim-layout}

::: {.sim-controls}

{{< include _controls.qmd >}}

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
max = 10                       // both axes run from 0 to max
isoquants = levels.flatMap(q => isoquant(q, p, max))

// Label each isoquant just above where it crosses the 45-degree line, K = L.
labels = levels
  .map(q => ({q, x: (q / A) ** (1 / (a + b))}))
  .filter(d => d.x < max * 0.93)
```

$a + b =$ ${scale.toFixed(2)}: ${returns} returns to scale. ${bNote}

:::

::: {.sim-output}

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
Plot.plot({
  width: 560,
  height: 560,
  x: {label: "Labour, L", domain: [0, max], ticks: 5},
  y: {label: "Capital, K", domain: [0, max], ticks: 5},
  marks: [
    Plot.ruleX([0]),
    Plot.ruleY([0]),
    Plot.line(isoquants, {x: "L", y: "K", z: "q", stroke: "#4269d0", clip: true}),
    Plot.text(labels, {
      x: "x", y: "x", text: d => `q = ${d.q}`,
      textAnchor: "start", dx: 6, dy: -8
    })
  ]
})
```
